reason: Anterior segment dysgenesis defines ocular disease; the evidence does not establish common extraocular damage across this umbrella.
Breast and prostate, the stated sites of origin, are outside the 13 axes; no_axis is appropriate.
Pulmonary arterial disease belongs to cardiovascular. Dyspnea alone does not establish pulmonary tissue damage; associated diseases do not add axes.
Meningeal origin supports neurologic primary; common optic apparatus compression with visual loss supports ocular involvement. Location alone does not establish skeletal or endocrine disease.
Leg ulceration directly damages skin. The supplied evidence supports no additional axis.
Oxidative phosphorylation deficiency is metabolic; seizures/developmental delay in 2/3 and cardiomyopathy in 1/3 support neurologic and cardiovascular involvement.
Neurologic dysfunction and defining hair abnormalities support the primary axes. Strabismus/ptosis and skeletal deformities each occur in 2/2 assessed patients, supporting both involved axes.
Cardiomyopathy affects myocardium, which belongs to cardiovascular. The muscle-tissue parent does not establish skeletal muscle disease.

The metabolic biosynthesis defect, contractures and skin fragility support the primary axes. Common ocular dysfunction qualifies; other qualifying organs are acknowledged and omitted under the four-axis cap.
Localized subcutaneous tissue loss defines dermatologic disease. Systemic metabolic dysfunction is not characteristic of this subtype, so the parent's metabolic axis need not be retained.
